labels.name: Tier 2
labels.description: Lower priority issues / Nice to haves

repository.name: alembic
repository.description: A database migrations tool for SQLAlchemy.

issue.body:
**Migrated issue, originally created by Derek Harland ([@donkopotamus](https://github.com/donkopotamus))**

I wonder if it might be a nice enhancement to allow a revision to be a python package instead of being constrained to be a python module.

This may have a few advantages:

- if a revision consists of a lot of code, or support functions specific to that revision, it might be nicer to be able to split that amongst several files.

  - this is particularly the case for the base revision of a database, which could be large.

- it might allow for easier storage of symbolic names//tags for a revision. eg if we had a file structure something like:

    - `versions/<revision_number>/__init__.py`

        - upgrade/downgrade code goes here

    - `versions/<revision_number>/cfg.py`

        - the values of the up/down revisions could be stored in here

        - this means the revision tree could be analysed by only loading `cfg.py` for such revisions

        - a symbolic name for the revision could be in here etc.

(Postgresql)
It appears everywhere I have a constraint in my sqlalchemy code in which there is a unique constaint index alembic --autogenerate wants to remove it.

ie.
python code:
lead_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('crm_lead.id'), unique=True)

DataBase \d:
Indexes:
    "chat_pkey" PRIMARY KEY, btree (id)
    "chat_lead_id_key" UNIQUE CONSTRAINT, btree (lead_id)

INFO  [alembic.autogenerate.compare] Detected removed index 'chat_lead_id_key' on 'chat'

It appears alembic does not consider constraints as indexes, and psql does.

issue.title: nosuchtableerror on autogenerate (was: Feature proposal: Choose the schema to use for the migrations )

repository.name: alembic
repository.description: A database migrations tool for SQLAlchemy.

issue.body:
**Migrated issue, originally created by jean soula ([@jeansoula](https://github.com/jeansoula))**

Hello !

I was struggling to generate revision for one of my company's project and the workaround was to modify some code in `autogenerate/compare.py`.

Our changes can be found in the attached file (patch format).

## Context

My python app needs to manage data in a specific postgresql schema (let's call it "custom_schema"). Some tables in this schema have foreign key to other tables in schema "public" (and I don't want to apply migrations on the schema "public").

In order to achieve this, I added `SET local search_path to custom_schema` in my `env.py` file.

While running `alembic revision --autogenerate`, `sqlalchemy.exc.NoSuchTableError` was raised. After some investigations I realized that code in `autogenerate/compare.py` was comparing the state "custom_schema" with the "public" schema. Which made the migration crash (Tables in "public" were marked as "removed").

## Fix

The proposed patch fixes this behavious by adding an option "target_schema" to `context.configure` in `env.py`.

I'll be happy to discuss about this proposal.

----------------------------------------
Attachments: [patch.txt](../wiki/imported_issue_attachments/493/patch.txt)

issue.title: SQLAlchemy 1.3 long name truncation

labels.name: external SQLAlchemy issues
labels.description: the issue is in SQLAlchemy, not here in alembic

repository.name: alembic
repository.description: A database migrations tool for SQLAlchemy.

issue.body:
I have an existing database A. A has had an alembic migration applied in the past with `op.f('some_long_constraint_name')`, which PostgreSQL truncated to `some_long_constraint_`.

I have a new database B. Applying the schema using alembic means it has a constraint named `some_long_constr_f5b8`.

I can't write a future migration that drops this constraint that will work in both cases.

I also can't write an alembic migration to fix the old truncated name because that migration would not work on B.

Is the intended solution that I manually rename all my previously-truncated names to use the new 4-character hash? It might be worth a mention in the SQLAlchemy changelog, but maybe it's just me who didn't immediately see the connotations of the change.

issue.title: Redundant foreign keys during autogenerate

labels.name: external SQLAlchemy issues
labels.description: the issue is in SQLAlchemy, not here in alembic

repository.name: alembic
repository.description: A database migrations tool for SQLAlchemy.

issue.body:
This is somewhat related to #519 except that the table names are in Title case.

Repeated execution of `alembic revision --autogenerate` then `alembic upgrade head` is continuously dropping all the existing foreign keys and regenerating them.

These are the versions:
SQLAlchemy - 1.3.5
Alembic - 1.0.11
MySQL - 5.7
PyMySQL - 0.9.3

```python
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy import MetaData
from sqlalchemy.schema import Column, ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.types import CHAR, VARCHAR

convention = {
  "ix": 'ix_%(column_0_label)s',
  "uq": "uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s",
  "ck": "ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s",
  "fk": "fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s",
  "pk": "pk_%(table_name)s"
}
meta = MetaData(naming_convention=convention)
Base = declarative_base(metadata=meta)

class Table1(Base):
	__tablename__ = "Table1"
	id = Column(CHAR(36), primary_key=True)
	name = Column(VARCHAR(255))

class Table2(Base):
	__tablename__ = "Table2"
	id = Column(CHAR(36), primary_key=True)
	name = Column(VARCHAR(255), unique=True)
	table1_id = Column(CHAR(36), ForeignKey("Table1.id"))
```

I find that it is happening due to mismatch in signature calculation. 

https://github.com/sqlalchemy/alembic/blob/f723827c82dfdb1145f3c73a88ad61bda1ca8d7f/alembic/autogenerate/compare.py#L997-L998

At the lines above, here are the signatures in my tests:

For `conn_fk_by_sig`:
`(None, 'Table2', ('table1_id',), None, 'table1', ('id',), None, None, 'not deferrable')`

For `metadata_fks_by_sig`:
`(None, 'Table2', ('table1_id',), None, 'Table1', ('id',), None, None, 'not deferrable')`

Notice that the difference is only in the case of the referred table (`table1` and `Table1`). 

When I edited [the class](https://github.com/sqlalchemy/alembic/blob/f723827c82dfdb1145f3c73a88ad61bda1ca8d7f/alembic/autogenerate/compare.py#L384)(`_fk_constraint_sig`) to convert all referred table names to lowercase, it worked fine.

How can I fix this?
